No route-count change, no DB/migration/CI/systemd/template/i18n change. origin/main..HEAD is empty (zero commits).

evidence: backend/tests/test_wecom_events.py::test_post_valid_signature_acknowledges_and_dispatches_worker_and_media (line 220): valid signature + <Encrypt> -> 200 'ok', worker dispatch recorded exactly once.

backend/tests/test_wecom_events.py::test_post_malformed_or_unsigned_input_never_dispatches (line 257, 5 cases missing_encrypt/malformed_cdata/malformed_xml/non_utf8_encrypt/invalid_signature): 400/403, worker_dispatches == [] and media dispatched == [].

backend/tests/test_wecom_events.py::test_post_missing_required_query_parameters_never_dispatches (line 280): 422, no dispatch. backend/tests/test_wecom_events.py::test_post_does_not_dispatch_without_an_active_callback_tenant (line 430): 503, no dispatch.

POST handler backend/app/routers/wecom_events.py:260-271 extracts <Encrypt> (structure) then verifies SHA1 signature (line 269-271) BEFORE tenant resolution/dispatch; dispatch at :281-283; every failure path raises before dispatch. POST never consumes/decrypts the event body (RND-105 merged contract: signature over raw encrypted content; the worker fetches data itself). The decrypt-failure surface (GET echostr) is unchanged and regression-covered by test_get_malformed_request_data_is_always_safe_400 (9 cases) and test_get_accepts_wecom_padding_larger_than_an_aes_block (16 cases).

Failed requests obtain no worker lock and produce no archive side effect: dispatch_archive_worker is only reachable after structure+signature+tenant checks; lock acquire happens inside dispatch (backend/app/services/archive_worker_trigger.py:62-66).

backend/tests/test_wecom_events.py::test_post_returns_before_the_shared_worker_finishes (line 360): blocking worker double with threading.Event barriers; asserts response.status_code == 200 and started.is_set() while not finished.is_set(), then releases; proves handler returned while worker still incomplete (barrier, not just HTTP 200).

Runtime smoke B (real machinery): dispatch_archive_worker returned ACCEPTED in ~2ms while the real subprocess worker (2s sleep) was still running; worker runs observed == 1 under a 20-call burst; lock free after completion. Full output: 'SMOKE B PASS' EXIT=0.
No BackgroundTasks dependency on the callback path: dispatch starts a daemon thread (backend/app/services/archive_worker_trigger.py:55-78) so the ack is independent of worker completion.

Callback dispatch chain: wecom_events.py:281 -> dispatch_archive_worker -> run_archive_worker_once (archive_worker_trigger.py:35-52) -> subprocess [sys.executable, backend/scripts/run_archive_worker_once.py] cwd=backend (archive_worker_trigger.py:38-42, _WORKER_SCRIPT :23).

Manual path now uses the same seam: backend/app/routers/sync.py:91-94 _run_archive_worker delegates to run_archive_worker_once; sync subprocess/Path/sys imports removed (diff -3 lines). backend/tests/test_sync_api.py::test_manual_worker_uses_the_shared_archive_worker_seam (line 178) and backend/tests/test_archive_worker_trigger.py::test_manual_and_callback_paths_share_the_worker_entrypoint (line 12) pin the identical argv/cwd/check=False invocation.

Timer path unchanged: deploy/systemd/wecom-archive-worker.service:11 ExecStart runs the same backend/scripts/run_archive_worker_once.py. Sync -> decrypt/normalization order preserved inside the shared script (run_archive_worker_once.py:174-176); no subprocess/SQL/business-step copy in the callback layer.

Same actual filesystem lock: callback/manual/timer all run backend/scripts/run_archive_worker_once.py, which owns the fcntl.flock on WORKER_LOCK_PATH or the shared default /srv/apps/wecom-archive-365/shared/run/wecom-archive-worker.lock (run_archive_worker_once.py:54-81, :160-171); systemd service uses the same script and env (wecom-archive-worker.service:10-11).

Runtime smoke A: with the real flock held, the real worker script printed 'archive_worker lock already held; exiting' and exited 0 (safe no-op) - WORKER_UNDER_LOCK EXIT=0; no overlapping worker cycle can start.

callback/callback concurrency: process-local coalescing lock (archive_worker_trigger.py:24, :62-78) plus cross-process flock; backend/tests/test_archive_worker_trigger.py::test_burst_is_coalesced_and_dispatch_returns_before_worker_finishes (line 46): 20 dispatches -> exactly 1 run, 20 SKIPPED; smoke B reproduced the same against the real subprocess.
callback vs already-locked worker/timer: the flock no-op contract means the second trigger's subprocess exits 0 immediately - at most one real worker cycle runs.

Structural bound: dispatch_archive_worker does a non-blocking acquire of a single module-level threading.Lock and starts at most one daemon thread named wecom-archive-worker-trigger; every further call returns SKIPPED (archive_worker_trigger.py:62-66). No queue, no unbounded thread/process/future/task growth.

Stress-style focused test: test_burst_is_coalesced_and_dispatch_returns_before_worker_finishes (line 46) fires 20 dispatches against a blocking worker and asserts runs == [1], all SKIPPED, then finished.wait + _dispatch_lock.acquire(timeout=1) proves resource release after completion.
Runtime smoke B: 20-dispatch burst against the real subprocess -> exactly 1 worker run; _dispatch_lock acquirable after completion (lock free).
Failure path releases the guard: test_dispatch_start_failure_releases_the_coalescing_guard (line 80) - thread.start() raising releases the lock so later dispatches are not wedged.

Accept-time failure is not faked as success: thread.start() failure -> ArchiveWorkerDispatch.FAILED -> 503 'Callback worker unavailable' (wecom_events.py:281-283); backend/tests/test_wecom_events.py::test_post_dispatch_failure_is_not_acknowledged (line 391) asserts 503 and no media dispatch.

Background worker failure is safely observable and does not modify the already-returned response: run_archive_worker_once returns False on exception or non-zero exit and logs only 'archive_worker result=failed' (archive_worker_trigger.py:43-49); the callback ack was already sent (response immutable).

No payload/secret/command args/traceback leakage: test_worker_failure_is_observable_without_exception_text (line 31) asserts sentinel exception text absent from logs; test_dispatch_failure_does_not_leak_request_data (line 413) recursively asserts sentinels absent from response.json() and all captured log messages.
Timer path untouched by this diff (deploy/systemd/wecom-archive-worker.service and .timer not in git status; ExecStart/schedule unchanged: OnCalendar=*:0/5).

Manual path behavior-preserving refactor: sync.py _run_archive_worker previously subprocess-ran the same script and marked failure on non-zero exit; now delegates to run_archive_worker_once() with identical semantics (exception or non-zero -> _mark_worker_failed). Regression test test_manual_worker_uses_the_shared_archive_worker_seam (line 178); existing sync-now tests (202/cooldown/already_running) still pass.

Same worker + same flock for timer/manual/callback (see AC-3/AC-4 evidence); lock-held and fatal-failure contracts unchanged (worker script untouched, exit 0 no-op / exit 1 fatal per run_archive_worker_once.py:19-22).

The diff touches only dispatch wiring: wecom_events.py POST handler, sync.py helper, and the new service module. No change to cursor/dedup/decrypt/normalization/revoke/media/ingest logic; backend/scripts/run_archive_worker_once.py, sync_wecom_archive_once.py, decrypt_wecom_messages_once.py, and all media/ingest modules are untouched (git status shows only the 6 RND-107 files).

Repeated/duplicate callbacks cannot create duplicate business records: a burst yields one worker cycle (test_burst... runs == [1]; smoke B runs == 1), and an already-running worker is a flock no-op, so the single-cycle worker's own cursor/dedup semantics are preserved.

Callback resolves the env-scoped corp to its active tenant only: _active_tenant_for_corp(_get_corp_id()) filters TenantWecomConfig by that corp_id + is_active (wecom_events.py:172-185); the resolved tenant_id stays in-process, is never logged, and is never passed to the worker (dispatch takes no tenant argument - archive_worker_trigger.py:62).

Worker is environment-scoped (single WECOM_CORP_ID, same as the manual path's existing guard sync.py:134-136); no cross-tenant read/select/print of other tenants' configs, credentials, or data in callback, config, worker, or logs.

tenant_id is used only for the pre-existing RND-172 media dispatch trigger (wecom_events.py:287-290), unchanged behavior. Logs contain no tenant ids (fixed allowlist events, wecom_events.py:50-64). Deployment shape is single-corp env-scoped (runbook docs/wecom_archive_worker_runbook.md); noted as a deployment fact, not a defect.

API responses are fixed strings only: 'ok', 'Invalid callback request', 'Invalid signature', 'Callback configuration error', 'Callback worker unavailable' (wecom_events.py:211/217/226/258/264/267/271/279/283).

Logs are fixed allowlist events: wecom_callback accepted/rejected reason=<enum>, archive_worker result=failed|completed, archive_worker trigger=accepted|skipped|dispatch_failed (wecom_events.py:61-64, archive_worker_trigger.py:44-51/65/77/80).

Subprocess argv is [sys.executable, script_path] only - no token, key, tenant, corp, or query data (archive_worker_trigger.py:38-42); verified by test_manual_and_callback_paths_share_the_worker_entrypoint.

Recursive sentinel tests per docs/agent-data-minimization.md: _SENTINELS (14 entries incl. SENTINEL_SECRET, /sentinel/fs/path, SENTINEL_TRACEBACK) asserted absent from response.json() and all log messages in test_dispatch_failure_does_not_leak_request_data, test_callback_business_logs_are_fixed_info_events_without_request_data, test_worker_failure_is_observable_without_exception_text, test_dispatch_start_failure_releases_the_coalescing_guard.
Uvicorn access-log query redaction covers the callback path (app/main.py:55-70 _RedactOAuthCallbackQueryFilter; test_access_log_filter_redacts_wecom_event_queries_and_preserves_other_paths line 339).
backend/tests/test_architecture_boundary.py EXIT=0, 25 passed.

Callback layer does not copy worker/sync/decrypt implementation: it delegates to the shared script; sync/decrypt orchestration stays in run_archive_worker_once.py:174-176.
